To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there is no correlation between the antioxydative and the antiradikal activity of substances under investigation.

(1) The antioxidant and antiradial activities of classic antioxidants and blockers of the Ca(2+) channel are determined; (2) There is a lack of correlation between the antioxidant and antiradiacal activities of the substances under investigation; (3) The antioxidant properties of pharmacologically active substances should be evaluated comprehensively.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of antiradical, antioxidative and cytotoxic activities of the following compounds: (i) phenolic antioxidants: 2,6-di-tert-butyl-p-cresol (BHT), 2,2′-dithiobis-(4-tert-octylphenol) (DTBP), 4-hydroxy-2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidine-1-oxyl (TEMPOL),
the antioxidant properties of the substances used as blockers of calcium channels and with the antiradicals of phenolic compounds.
the study of the antioxidative and antiradicals properties of the drugs used in the treatment of ischemic heart diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antioxidant activity of a substance is a function of many factors.

the antioxidant activity of the substances under investigation is a complex phenomenon, which depends not only on the antiradial and antioxidative activities, but also on their other physiological properties, such as the effect on Ca(2+)-channels and the ability to inhibit phospholipase A(2) and cyclooxygenase.

the antioxidants are a heterogeneous group of compounds, and the antioxidant activity of the substances is not only determined by their ability to donate hydrogen atoms to radicals but also by the mechanism of the radical scavenging and the ability to chelate metal ions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the antioxidants and Ca(2+) channel blockers are able to inhibit the lipid peroxidation in the liver microsomes.

the antioxidant activity of a compound is not always directly related to its antiradical properties, and that the antioxidant activity is not only a function of the antiradial capacity but also depends on its ability to scavenge the lipid radicals and to chelate transition metals.

there is a necessity of complex study of antioxidative and antiradial activity of substances under investigation in the model systems of liver microsomal membranes and erythrocytes, which would allow to evaluate the antioxidative properties of pharmacological substances in the conditions of their physiological activity and to determine their possible role in the prevention and therapy of free radical diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antioxidant activity of a compound does not correlate with its antiradical properties.
it is important to understand the mechanisms of antioxidant action in the context of their chemical structure and the nature of the biological systems in which they are used.
it is important to consider the antioxidant properties of drugs when developing new therapies for neurodegenerative disorders.
